# Office-design maintenance and historical input

Re-authored on 2026-10-13: the workflow body, token-contract reference, validator, its tests and the four theme palettes were rewritten from the actual PDF, XLSX, DOCX and PPTX interfaces. The palettes are newly designed (every text pair at least 4.5:1, chart colours at least 3:1 against the background). Compatibility is kept deliberately: the Skill frontmatter and filenames, the required token keys and their order, theme IDs, and the validator CLI, exit codes and JSON output shapes; the validator and a differential fuzz against the previous implementation showed no behavioural differences. A line comparison with the imported snapshot finds these shares of non-blank lines: SKILL.md 23%, validate_theme.py 17%, tests 22%, each theme file 6% (the required keys), token-schema.md 0%. Current maintenance is not a claim that all repository content is original Firefly work.

Historical office-design input is traced by the distributed `license-provenance.json` and `LICENSE-NOTICES.md` to Playa-0v0/Cyrene-Agent, including commit `edca2be98b1899769d18faa7239ba7b398ef13c6`. The verified MIT revision is `734bfeeab97b0cdaf5a29ee8fd8f0d61efb88948`; its complete license and `Copyright (c) 2026 Playa` notice remain in `../../licenses/upstream-contributions-MIT.txt`. Preserve that license and the distributed provenance records with this directory. Historical per-file hashes describe historical input; they are not byte-identity assertions for these rewritten files.

This scoped maintenance does not rewrite historical provenance records, relicense adjacent document Skills, or clear any unresolved source review. The current formal snapshot and `license-provenance.json.currentDistribution` identify these maintained files by hash. MiniMax, other upstream authors and external programs retain their own applicable notices and licenses.
